findings:
🟠 [timeout-source-overload] MUST-FIX Plain `--timeout` with no Mission contract now sets `TIMEOUT_SOURCE="caller_within_wall"` (pre-preflight fallback block), so the result JSON and manifest write `timeout_source: "caller_within_wall"` for a run where no contract existed; that value previously meant "caller value accepted within a contract's wall budget", so manifest/result consumers will infer a contract was in play. Smallest fix: assign a distinct enum value for the no-contract case (e.g. `TIMEOUT_SOURCE="caller"`) in that fallback block; every enforcement predicate already keys only on non-emptiness, so `caller`/`contract_wall`/`caller_within_wall` all enforce and `default` stays unenforced.
🟠 [fired-path-holds-token-kills-dead-pgid] MUST-FIX On the timed-out path `_wait_worker_with_watchdog` returns from `wait "$rp"` (worker died at SIGTERM) but does not remove the token before `wait "$WATCHDOG_PID"`; the watchdog's grace loop only exits when the token is gone, so it always sleeps the full 10s and then unconditionally sends `kill -KILL -$WORKER_SID` to a process group whose members already exited. That is exactly the recycled-pid/pgid hazard the spec forbids (and adds 10s to every timeout even when TERM sufficed). Smallest fix: on the `.fired` branch, `rm -f "$WATCHDOG_TOKEN_FILE"` immediately after `wait "$rp"` returns and before waiting on `WATCHDOG_PID`, so the loop's `[ -f "$tok" ] || exit 0` short-circuits and SIGKILL is only sent while the worker is still alive; keep `reap_container` as the survivor sweep.
🟡 [early-cancel-sleeper-leak] MUST-FIX In `_cancel_worker_watchdog`, if the worker exits before the watchdog subshell has written `${tok}.sleeppid` (fast worker, e.g. the `HETERO_TEST_SLEEP=0` no-stray case), the sleeper is not killed and the subshell is then SIGTERMed while blocked in `wait`, orphaning the setsid'd `hetero-wall-watchdog-<tag> sleep N` process for the full timeout — a stray sleeper after a normal completion, which the spec forbids and `assert_r1_no_stray_watchdog` will flake on. Smallest fix: inside the watchdog subshell set `sp=""` then `trap 'kill "${sp:-}" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM` before forking the sleeper and assign `sp=$!` right after; and in `_cancel_worker_watchdog`, after killing/waiting `WATCHDOG_PID`, re-read `.sleeppid` (or `pkill -f "hetero-wall-watchdog-${tag}"` using the unique token tag) as the belt-and-braces sweep.
🔵 [setsid-wait-ppid-race] CUT/FOLLOW-UP On the `setsid --wait` path `WORKER_SID` is read via a single `ps --ppid "$rp"` immediately after backgrounding; if the lookup runs before setsid has forked, `WORKER_SID` falls back to `$rp` (the supervisor, not a group leader), so the watchdog's `kill -TERM -$rp` fails and the fallback `kill -TERM $rp` kills only the supervisor, leaving the worker alive while `timed_out=true`. Pre-existing capture logic, now load-bearing for kill targeting; harden later with a short bounded retry of the ppid lookup. Excluded because the diff did not introduce it and `reap_container` still sweeps survivors.
🔵 [set-m-job-notices] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The no-setsid fallback enables `set -m` in a non-interactive shell, which makes bash print `[1]+ Terminated …` job notices to stderr on kill; stdout JSON is unaffected. Cosmetic, excluded from this version.
🔵 [red-comment-garbled-line] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The RED evidence block in the new test contains a self-correcting line ("expected '' got 'false' wait — actually expected 'false' got ''"); tidy the wording. Evidence still demonstrates RED against base; excluded as non-functional.
🔵 [no-stray-test-global-pgrep] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `assert_r1_no_stray_watchdog` uses `pgrep -f 'hetero-wall-watchdog'` across the whole host, so a sleeper from a concurrently running suite would produce a false failure, and on hosts without setsid the untagged `sleep` fallback is invisible to the check. Scope the match to this run's token tag when convenient; excluded because it does not affect production behaviour.
